result.summary: The street features wide, well-maintained sidewalks on both sides with street trees and lighting, creating a generally comfortable pedestrian environment. However, the presence of trolley tracks in the roadway and the lack of marked crossings or dedicated cycling infrastructure increases the risk of conflict between different road users.

hazards.name: Trolley tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway pose a significant tripping hazard for pedestrians crossing mid-block and a crash risk for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway running parallel to traffic lanes.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: The absence of visible crosswalks over a long stretch of street may encourage unsafe mid-block crossings in an area with high pedestrian potential.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk, potentially with a pedestrian refuge island, to provide a safe and legal crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Dedicated Bike Lanes
interventions.description: Implement marked or protected bike lanes to separate cyclists from both motor vehicle traffic and the hazardous trolley tracks.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk and a dedicated bike lane, providing good separation from vehicular traffic. However, the presence of a large blank building frontage reduces natural surveillance and creates a less engaging streetscape. While the infrastructure is generally in good condition, the lack of immediate crossing facilities and active street-level features limits the overall pedestrian experience.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The large windowless concrete wall provides no natural surveillance, which can decrease the perceived safety of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, the large concrete building.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Facilities
hazards.description: There are no marked pedestrian crossings or curb ramps visible in the immediate mid-block area, requiring pedestrians to walk to the next intersection.

interventions.title: Active Frontage
interventions.description: Incorporate public art, murals, or architectural lighting on the blank wall to improve the pedestrian experience and safety through increased visual interest.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with ADA-compliant curb ramps to provide a safe and convenient crossing point for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection featuring multiple travel lanes and integrated trolley tracks. While high-visibility continental crosswalks and sidewalks are present, the significant crossing distance and complex traffic environment pose risks to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must traverse multiple lanes of traffic and trolley tracks, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: The embedded tracks in the roadway can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians or catch bicycle wheels.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised refuge island in the center of the wide crossing to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk with street trees, lighting, and a transit shelter. While the infrastructure is robust, the presence of a large parked vehicle creates a visual obstruction that may hinder sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked vehicle
hazards.description: A large white van parked at the curb obscures the view of the roadway for pedestrians and the view of the sidewalk for drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, parked along the curb.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the ends of the parking lane to improve visibility and shorten crossing distances if a crossing were to be installed.

interventions.title: Enhanced Street Furniture Buffer
interventions.description: Formalize the furniture zone with additional planters or permanent fixtures to clearly delineate the pedestrian realm from the parking and travel lanes.
